Yury Polozov discusses legislative priorities and recent transportation law in New Hampshire
M. O. Isaac
Yury Polozov, a public figure active on social media, recently posted a series of tweets addressing political and legislative issues in New Hampshire. His comments ranged from criticisms of claims made by Democratic opponents to updates on legislative actions concerning transportation planning.
On August 17, 2026, Polozov commented on differing statistics used by critics of the Education Freedom Account (EFA) program, stating, "It’s hilarious, Dems who hate EFA for caring parents like to make this claim but it’s a different number each time, 70, 90, I even saw a baseless claim of 95%!"
The following day, August 18, he solicited input from followers regarding possible veto overrides in the state legislature: "What vetoes from the Republican Governor should I try to override tomorrow? Do you want: • Fresh local meat? • Two more years of road planning + higher tolls for drivers without E-ZPass? • Or should I sustain the veto on a potentially questionable expansion of the R&D tax"
On August 19, Polozov announced progress on transportation legislation: "Ten-Year Transportation Improvement Plan is Now Law! I voted for HB 2026 (New Hampshire’s Ten-Year Transportation Improvement Plan for 2027–2036), and we successfully overrode the governor’s veto. Two projects in my district can now move forward: • Hooksett: Intersection"
The Education Freedom Account program referenced by Polozov has been debated among New Hampshire lawmakers and advocates. Supporters argue it provides greater educational choice for families, while opponents question its impact on public education funding. Legislative discussions around road infrastructure and tolling are ongoing topics within the state government.
HB 2026 refers to New Hampshire's official plan guiding transportation investments over a ten-year period. The plan typically includes major roadway improvements and infrastructure upgrades across various districts in the state.
